page: Microsoft Azure E32-16ads_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. This virtual machine is provisioned with 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The hardware configuration features a high memory-to-core ratio, providing 256.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 16.0 GB per core. It includes 1890 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage, but does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance. The server ranks in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core score, and single-threaded text processing. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory performance is strong, with the Passmark memory score placing in the top 25%, while uncached memory read and write bandwidth remain average. For language model tasks, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds with small 135M models, but drops to the bottom 25% for prompt processing on large 70B models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E32-16ads_v7 offers high memory density and fast local NVMe storage relative to its 16-vCPU compute allocation, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads. However, the average multi-core scaling relative to its single-core strength suggests a tradeoff where parallelized compute tasks may not scale as efficiently as memory-intensive operations. This profile is suited for memory-intensive databases, caching layers, text processing pipelines, and small-scale language model inference.
